thread:
rachel: paging oncall 78: deploy flagged as progressive (10% canary) for model-serving-prod. We're seeing a steady rise in 502/504s and pods flapping in the canary cohort. tagging oncall.

pager-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident INC-2026-0789 created. Notifying oncall-sre.

diego: i'm oncall. any customer reports?

account-bot: 3 customer support tickets opened referencing intermittent 502 on /v1/generate and embeddings endpoints (tickets: #4582 #4583 #4584). Top affected: data-annotators-inc.

mina: looking at kube: several canary pods report CrashLoopBackOff with 'permission denied mounting volume' and the gateway returns upstream connection reset. sample log from init container:
```
2026-05-10T11:12:02Z INFO validating model cache dir
2026-05-10T11:12:02Z ERROR mkdir /cache/models: permission denied
2026-05-10T11:12:02Z ERROR failed to create cache dir, exiting
```

rachel: did we change securityContext or the PVC?

diego: deploy pipeline changed the CSI driver params last week (
--fsGroup=1337 -> removed). The new image expects writeable /cache/models, but the pod's securityContext now defaults to runAsNonRoot with no fsGroup, so volume is root-owned and init container can't write. Worse, the canary manifest also referenced a new PSP/PodSecurityPolicy alias (psp-modeling-v2) that doesn't exist in this cluster because we recently removed PSPs and rely on OPA/Gatekeeper constraints now; the mismatch caused admission to mutate securityContext unexpectedly.

mina: interesting. I also see HPA chatter: the HPA targeting the canary was configured with a custom external metric name 'inference_queue_length' but our metrics adapter changed last deploy (adapter now exposes 'queue_length_v2'). So HPA failed to scale canary pods up during failures. That amplified impact.

eng-bot: Cluster event: node-21 cordoned at 11:10:14 UTC for kernel patch; drain initiated, 5 pods evicted.

rachel: great timing. So root causes: securityContext/CSI param mismatch -> init permission errors; HPA external metric name mismatch -> no scale-up; node drain -> pod churn.

mina: mitigation plan: 1) stop canary traffic by toggling feature flag; 2) scale canary deployment to zero; 3) if needed hotfix securityContext in canary image or create compat fsGroup via init job; 4) pause node drain for remaining rotation window.

diego: toggling LaunchDarkly flag now: ldcli set inference_canary_percent 0 --env prod.

diego: done 705f: LaunchDarkly inference_canary_percent -> 0. Traffic routed to stable.

rachel: scaling down canary pods:
```
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/model-serving-canary --replicas=0
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=model-serving -o wide
```

mina: paused node maintenance by messaging infra runbook. they acknowledged and abated the drain for node-21.

ops-bot: Node maintenance paused by @mina. Node-21 remains cordoned but not drained further.

account-bot: CS: ~650 failed requests, affecting 4 customers. Top impacted tenant notified.

diego: mitigation looks stable: error rate back to baseline after 7m. Gateway 5xx dropped off.

mina: next steps: short-term hotfix options: A) update canary manifest to set securityContext.fsGroup=1337 (quick but masks underlying mismatch), B) revert CSI param change in pipeline and force redeploy of canary image, or C) push an init step to chown /cache at runtime (less ideal). Which is fastest for safe redeploy?

rachel: prefer to revert pipeline CSI param change and re-run canary with correct fsGroup. That avoids guessing ownership changes. Diego, can you coordinate rollback in the pipeline?

diego: yes, rolling back the pipeline change now and will trigger a dry canary in staging first. I'll also open a PR to add a pre-deploy validation: verify required PSP/constraint references exist and validate HPA external metric names against metrics adapter.

mina: also adding CI guard: 'kubectl apply --dry-run=server' + 'kubectl auth can-i create/patch' checks for preflight. And HPA validation script to assert metric names.

rachel: CS comms drafted. We'll offer affected customers a follow-up once postmortem is done.

diego: incident summary for PD: root cause = deploy pipeline removed fsGroup/Csi param -> init containers couldn't write to model cache -> CrashLoopBackOff. Contributing factors = HPA external metric rename prevented auto scale, simultaneous node maintenance caused extra churn. Impact = P2, ~25m degraded service for subset of traffic, ~650 failed requests, 4 customers affected. Mitigation = feature flag toggle to 0%, scaled canary to 0, paused node maintenance, pipeline rollback triggered.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0789 assigned to diego. Next oncall: mina at 08:00 UTC.

rachel: assigning owners: diego -> rollback + pipeline PR; mina -> HPA validation + CI checks; rachel -> customer comms + postmortem write-up. Moving to postmortem channel. Closing active pager. :white_check_mark:
